question: The fall of which strategic Portuguese fort in 1622, captured by an alliance of the English East India Company and the Safavid dynasty of Persia, crippled the naval control of the Portuguese over the Persian Gulf?
explanation: The capture of Ormuz (Hormuz) in 1622 by a joint Anglo-Persian force was a major blow to the Portuguese. It stripped them of their key fortress guarding the entrance to the Persian Gulf, ended their ability to levy customs duties there, and marked the beginning of active Anglo-Dutch-Mughal-Persian alliances that dismantled the Portuguese cartaz system.
